item.title: These App Store hidden gems prove there’s still room for great software in the AI era
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Despite predictions that AI agents could make traditional apps obsolete, developers are shipping new software faster than ever. From smarter bookmarking tools and neighborhood marketplaces to digital pen pals and nature journals, here are the latest App Store finds worth adding to your Home Screen.

item.title: HBO Max embraces vertical video with a new ‘Shorts’ feed
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: HBO Max, like other streaming platforms, is rethinking content discovery as large libraries are making it hard for viewers to find something to watch and as audiences become accustomed to short-form content on platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels.

item.title: Saudi prince buys 5% stake in Lucid Motors
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The investment comes after speculation that Saudi Arabia may take Lucid Motors private -- which the EV maker has denied.

item.title: Data centers may face temporary power cuts to prevent blackouts on largest US grid
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: The decision arrives as the breakneck pace of data center construction has grid operators scrambling to generate power.

item.title: PayPal leaves the door open to a higher takeover offer following earnings beat
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: After reporting better-than-expected Q2 results, PayPal said it remains focused on its AI-driven turnaround, but would consider a deal that creates more value for shareholders.

item.title: Elon Musk’s X Money app is rolling out in the US
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Users get an X Visa debit card, which they can immediately add to Apple Pay and use to make instant peer-to-peer transfers within the app without fees or limits.

item.title: WhatsApp now lets you make calls using its web app
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Similar to the smartphone and desktop apps, the web app will support calling features such as screen-sharing and reactions.

item.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Since launching last year, the startup today has more than 8 million people using the open source or hosted version of its models, and now generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million.

item.title: Apple launches ‘Upgrade’ device leasing program in partnership with Klarna
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The rollout of the program comes as Apple has been struggling with supply chain issues related to "RAMageddon," which refers to the industry-wide shortage of memory chips that is driving up the price of hardware.

item.title: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410M compute deal with Amazon
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Recursive’s emphasis on self-improving AI systems means much of the budget that would traditionally go toward headcount and operations is put straight into compute, as the company seeks to automate its own product development process.

item.title: Granola launches an Apple Watch app
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Granola debuts an Apple Watch app for in-person note taking.

item.title: Lyft and Baidu enter London’s robotaxi battleground as testing begins
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Baidu's Apollo Go autonomous vehicles will be available on Freenow, the mobility network that Lyft acquired in 2025.

item.title: Cursor makes its biggest India push yet ahead of SpaceX acquisition with localized pricing
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Cursor says India is now its third-largest market globally and plans to expand local hiring and enterprise sales.

item.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Anthropic founder and CEO Dario Amodei made his views clear about open-weight models and China's growing AI capabilities.

item.title: Satya Nadella says companies that trust one AI for everything may not survive
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Companies without their own models — or without a layer of AI infrastructure known as AI gateways to separate their prompts from the model itself — will be in trouble, Nadella says.

item.title: Thea Energy lands $20M federal grant to build its magnets for fusion reactors
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fusion power startup Thea Energy snagged a $20 million award from ARPA-E to scale production of its high-temperature superconducting magnets.

item.title: As rivals chase acquisitions, Peacock bets on bundles through a new deal with YouTube
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The deal means content will be integrated into the YouTube experience, allowing viewers to discover and watch Peacock content without leaving the platform.

item.title: PSA: Your Claude shared chats and Artifacts may have ended up on Google
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
item.description: The issue appears to have originated from Claude’s “share chat” feature, which allows users to create links that enable anyone with the assigned URL view a conversation or project.

item.title: Microsoft launches its first cybersecurity model, plus a new agentic cybersecurity system
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Microsoft bolstered its AI cybersecurity offerings this week with the launch of its first AI security model and a new security platform.

item.title: Apple sued after alleged App Store crypto scam cost users $1.8M
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Apple is facing a lawsuit from three users who say they collectively lost more than $1.8 million after downloading a fraudulent crypto wallet from the App Store, challenging the company’s longstanding claims that its app review process keeps users safe from scams.
